subject: Private deployment control-plane reconnection — customer incident summary & remediation plan

Subject: Re: Strange failures in private deployment - agent disconnects

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We started seeing ~30% of our scheduled inference jobs fail around 07:45 PDT this morning. The agents in our private VPC were reporting repeated 'CONTROL_PLANE_UNREACHABLE' and a bunch of k8s probes restarted the agents. We pulled logs from one affected node and attached a small bundle (agent-logs-20260509.tar.gz).

Immediate impact: queued requests were dropped, and a handful of long-running requests timed out. No user data appears lost but throughput is severely degraded. Can you confirm whether this was an internal rollout on Redwood's end or something on our side? We can afford a short maintenance window this week but need clarity & timeline.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Platform Ops, SecuriHealth

Subject: Re: Strange failures in private deployment - agent disconnects

Tom / Vanessa — quick technical update from triage:
- What happened: during the configuration refresh we rolled a small helper that updates controller egress handling. A change to an iptables migration script accidentally removed a SNAT rule on control-plane-facing subnets for some private deployments. That caused agent heartbeats originating from the node IPs to be dropped at the control-plane ingress, resulting in CONTROL_PLANE_UNREACHABLE errors and agent restarts.

- How we verified: matched timestamps in the logs you attached with our rollout CI logs; reproduced the failure in a staging private VPC by re-running the migration step.

- Temporary mitigation (applied to affected nodes at 10:40 PDT): re-inserted the SNAT rule and restarted the control-plane webhook router. Agents resumed heartbeats; we observed normal request throughput return by ~11:05 PDT.

- Permanent fix: we have a patch that retracts the faulty iptables change and adds an automated validation in the rollout to check for SNAT presence. I’ve attached a small, conservative workaround script you can run on nodes if you prefer a customer-side mitigation while we schedule the official patch (workaround-iptables.sh).

Next steps: schedule a short (20–30m) maintenance window to apply the patch across your private agents; we prefer an out-of-hours window for minimal disruption.

— Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident recap & next steps — SecuriHealth private deployment (control-plane reconnection)

Tom — thank you for the coordination and for approving the maintenance window. This is a concise post-incident summary and next-action checklist. Please find a one-page recap attached (incident-recap-20260512.pdf) and links to our internal ticket for transparency.

Summary:
- Timeline: 07:30 PDT (05/09) control-plane helper rollout; 07:45–09:00 saw agent heartbeats drop; mitigation applied 10:40 PDT; normal service resumed ~11:05 PDT.
- Root cause: an iptables migration step removed a SNAT rule on control-plane subnets for a subset (≈12%) of private deployments during a helper rollout. This prevented agent heartbeats from reaching the control-plane router.
- Impact: transient failures for queued inference requests and scheduled jobs; no data exfiltration or data-loss observed.

Actions completed:
- Emergency mitigation applied (re-inserted SNAT rule).
- Out-of-hours patch applied 01:10 PDT (05/11) with smoke tests passing.
- Added automated pre-rollout validation to detect missing SNAT rules.

Follow-ups (owner / ETA):
- Formal RCA document with expanded logs: Dev Patel / 2026-05-13 EOD.
- Add workaround script to SecuriHealth runbook and provide signature of support-approval: Jordan Blake / 2026-05-13 12:00 PDT.
- Post-incident retro with product & infra to improve rollout gating: Neha Kapoor / 2026-05-18.

Rollback and safety: We kept a rollback image available throughout the patch window and did not need to rollback. We will retain a 2-hour monitoring hold after subsequent helper rollouts for your environment for the next 30 days.

Attached: incident-recap-20260512.pdf (1 page) — includes timeline, mitigations, and verification checklist.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute call this week to walk through the RCA and answer any questions. Please let me know times that work and we’ll set it up.

Thanks again — apologies for the disruption and we’ll follow up with the formal RCA by tomorrow EOD.

— Vanessa Ortiz
